page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; no margin notes; below the text a signature mark at the foot right.

main_text.p: egent. Cæterum ideo non putrescit ignis Aristoteli, quòd sit forma aliorum elementorum, quæ quidē ei materia sint: aut quia humido putredinis subiecto caret. Hac de causa terra simplex, sinceraq; putrescere nequit. Quapropter possunt putrescere sola aqua & aër: quando uidelicet hic non perflatur, illa uero non fluit. Tunc enim aliorū elementorum permistione, & externi caloris interuentu quodammodo putrescunt, & corrumpuntur. Plantæ & animalia, licet primùm corrumpetur diffolutione ficci ab humido, uti & formæ à materia: tamen tandem putrescūt: quoniam putredo est finis omnis, quæ natura constituuntur. Proptere a eam rectè opponit Aristotel. lib. 4. meteo. cap. 1. simplici generationi, quæ natura lis est & propria. Postremò putrescunt humores in animalium corporibus prohibita transpiratione. Quòd putredinis genus duplex constituit, Galenus libro primo de Differetiis febrium. Prius autem est, in quo natura uincit, quale in abscessibus apparet & est in febribus, quæ per se lethales non sunt. Huiusmodi putredo in abscessibus suppuratio dicitur, & imperfecta putredo; quoniam concoctioni coniuncta est. Poste rius

page.notes: Text is faint in places; the catchword-like "rius" at the foot is the start of the printed word "posterius" split by the signature line, rendered as printed. Doubtful readings: "Proptere a" may be a line-break artefact for "Proptereā"; "tandem" in "tamen tandem" is read from a faint word; "Quòd" and "quæ quidē" are as printed. Long s is plain s throughout. The phrase "Poste rius" is printed as a line-end split and the second part appears at the foot beside the signature.
